topic: The three main parts of a kitchen exhaust system: hood, duct and fan

slides.headline: Three parts. Miss one and the kitchen never clears.
slides.subline: The hood, the duct and the fan are one system, not three purchases.

slides.title: The hood captures
slides.intro: It sits over the cooking line and takes smoke, heat and grease away.

items.title: Canopy size
items.text: Narrower than the line, smoke slips past the edges.

items.title: Grease filters
items.text: Grease stops here, so clean them on a routine.

items.title: Fitting height
items.text: Too high, and smoke spreads before it is caught.

slides.note_text: Most escaping smoke leaves at the open ends of a canopy.

slides.title: The duct carries, the fan pulls
slides.intro: A duct without a fan is just a metal box.

items.title: Duct route
items.text: Short, straight runs beat long ones with bends.

items.title: The fan
items.text: Sized to hood and duct. Too small clears nothing.

items.title: Discharge
items.text: Air must leave the building, not the ceiling void.

slides.headline: Three parts. One system. One supplier.
slides.subline: Send your layout and we will check all three.

caption_en:
Hood, duct, fan. Most kitchens buy the three separately, then wonder why the room still fills with smoke.

The hood captures, the duct carries, the fan pulls. Each one limits what the other two can do. A strong fan under a narrow canopy still loses smoke at the edges, and a wide hood on a long twisting duct still feels weak at the cooking line.

Before you replace anything, look at all three together. We plan, manufacture and install complete exhaust systems in Doha, in the steel grade that suits each part.
